title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Further Strengthening Administrative Adjudication Work
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Further Strengthening Administrative Adjudication Work

Fa [2004] No. 33

High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

Since the implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law, people's courts at all levels have earnestly fulfilled their duties in administrative adjudication, lawfully adjudicated a large number of administrative cases, reviewed and executed a large number of non-litigation administrative enforcement cases, actively protected the lawful rights and interests of citizens, legal persons, and other organizations, effectively supervised and supported administrative organs in law-based administration, achieved remarkable results in various adjudicative tasks, and played a prominent role in the great process of governing the country according to law and building a socialist country under the rule of law. Currently, China's administrative adjudication work is entering a new historical stage. The Sixteenth National Congress of the Communist Party of China established the important goal of building a moderately prosperous society in all respects, requiring administrative adjudication to play a greater role in building a sound socialist market economy system, advancing the process of socialist democracy and legal system, and promoting socialist political civilization; China's accession to the World Trade Organization requires administrative adjudication to undertake new judicial review functions, the field of administrative adjudication continues to expand, and its social influence is increasing day by day; administrative adjudication is closely related to the vital interests of the people, who place high expectations on administrative adjudication work; the role of administrative adjudication in protecting the practical interests of the people is becoming increasingly prominent, and the responsibility of administrative adjudication is growing. However, there remains a considerable gap between the current state of administrative adjudication work and the requirements of the new situation and new tasks. Administrative adjudication work has not received the attention it deserves, and its constitutional and legal status has not been fully implemented; the organizational structure for administrative adjudication is not yet sound, and the quality of the administrative adjudication judge corps needs further improvement; the judicial environment for administrative adjudication is unsatisfactory, and there are still considerable obstacles to carrying out administrative adjudication work. In order to fully leverage the functions of administrative adjudication and further strengthen administrative adjudication work, it is hereby notified as follows:

1. Effectively enhance the understanding of the importance of administrative adjudication work. Administrative adjudication is a sacred duty conferred on people's courts by the Constitution and laws, and is an important aspect of the adjudicative work of people's courts. Doing a good job in administrative adjudication is a concrete requirement for people's courts to implement the important thought of the "Three Represents," an important manifestation of practicing justice for the people, and a key yardstick for measuring the level of modern rule-of-law awareness of courts at all levels. Leaders of courts at all levels, especially the top leader, must fully recognize the practical and historical significance of administrative adjudication work from the perspective of implementing the "Three Represents," from the perspective of governing the country according to law and building a socialist country under the rule of law, and from the perspective of implementing the requirements of seeking truth and being pragmatic and justice for the people, and actively take various practical and feasible measures to do a good job in administrative adjudication.

2. Vigorously strengthen the construction of the administrative adjudication judge corps. Administrative adjudication involves the review of the legality of administrative acts, judicial supervision and checks on administrative power, and is an important window for demonstrating the level of rule of law and the image of the court corps. It requires administrative adjudication judges to have high political quality and professional competence. Courts at all levels must, in light of the characteristics of administrative adjudication work, strengthen the construction of the administrative adjudication judge corps, fully staff administrative adjudication personnel in accordance with legal provisions, and promptly eliminate the current phenomenon of "one-person tribunals" or "two-person tribunals" that cannot legally form a collegial panel and where the adjudicative organization structure is unsound. The appointment of the division chief, deputy division chief, and presiding judges of the administrative adjudication division of courts at all levels must adhere to high standards and strict requirements. Administrative adjudication personnel should have relative stability, and attention should be paid to retaining key professionals. The division chief of the administrative adjudication division should be a member of the adjudication committee. The initiative of courts at all levels shall be fully utilized, training efforts shall be intensified, and the overall professional level of administrative adjudication personnel shall be improved as soon as possible.

3. Actively carry out innovation in the administrative adjudication system. Administrative adjudication has particularities different from other adjudication work. Courts at all levels shall, in accordance with the overall deployment of judicial reform by the people's courts, and based on the characteristics and patterns of administrative adjudication work, actively reform and innovate the administrative adjudication system and working mechanisms, strengthen the protection of the right to sue, improve litigation procedures, strengthen measures to make administrative adjudication accessible and convenient for the people, effectively promote the in-depth development of various tasks, and strive to elevate administrative adjudication work to a new level in the short term.

4. Strive to create a favorable judicial environment for administrative adjudication. Courts at all levels shall, based on local conditions, through methods such as regular special briefings and conducting inspections of the implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law, actively and consciously accept leadership from Party committees and supervision from people's congresses, seek support from governments, lawfully eliminate various phenomena of substituting words for law, using power to override law, and illegal interference in administrative adjudication work, put an end to "officials protecting each other," seriously eliminate various "local policies" that hinder the acceptance and adjudication of administrative cases, optimize the judicial environment, and ensure judicial fairness. Care must always be taken to maintain the neutrality and independence of administrative adjudication. When encountering phenomena such as local requirements for "joint offices" or "joint law enforcement" with relevant departments, efforts should be actively made to persuade the relevant parties. Judicial publicity of administrative adjudication work should be strengthened to enhance understanding and comprehension of administrative adjudication work among all sectors of society and create a favorable social atmosphere.

March 17, 2004
